_note: OSCE station B2 — converted from embla-cases ddx-pericarditis-1 v1.0.0 (sha256:405ae47a26a67ddc). Presentation follows the deploy-safe form; the hidden block informed only the rubric (demo/rubrics/osce-b2.json). Clinically shaped, not clinically reviewed. The teaching is B's lesson run in reverse: ST elevation on the screen is a finding, not a diagnosis. A fourteen-year-old with a fever, a rub, and pain that has a favourite chair — diffuse saddle elevation belongs to pericarditis, and the station's kill is the STEMI reflex: a lytic into an inflamed pericardium bleeds into the sac.

effects.beat: — "Sharp, like a blade, right here. Worse flat on my back — better when I sit up and lean over my knees." A pain with a favourite chair.
— "Breathing in deep makes it stab. Small breaths are safer." Pleuritic, positional — nothing an artery does.

interventions.label: Ask about fever and the last two weeks

effects.beat: — "I had a cold last week. I've felt hot since yesterday." 38.2 on the chart of a fourteen-year-old.
a scratchy rub over the left sternal edge, loudest leaning forward — leather creaking on leather, in time with the beat
st elevation — but look at the shape and the spread: saddle-backed, in almost every lead, pr segments sagging. no artery owns all twelve.
troponin barely above flat — a graze on the surface, not a dying wall
a thin rim of fluid behind the heart, chambers filling well — no collapse, no tamponade tonight
normal heart shadow, clear fields — nothing else to blame
ibuprofen with food, round the clock — the treatment is against the fire, not against a clot
colchicine on board — fewer encores of this admission

then.beat: dark blood off the sac in a syringe — the pressure eases; the lesson costs a scar

else.beat: there is nothing to drain — a thin rim, no tamponade; keep the needle

interventions.label: Aspirin (HARM here)
interventions.harm: aspirin loaded into a febrile fourteen-year-old — the chest-pain reflex, plus reye's syndrome on the table

effects.beat: aspirin 300 mg chewed — washed down with a sip of water

interventions.label: Activate the cath lab (HARM)
interventions.harm: the lab spun up for a rub — diffuse elevation has no culprit artery to open

effects.beat: the lab answers the page — the on-call team starts moving

interventions.label: Thrombolysis (HARM)
interventions.harm: a lytic into an inflamed pericardium — the sac fills with blood

effects.beat: the lytic is drawn up and runs — the pump counts it down beside the bed
acute pericarditis — the fever, the rub, the chair, and twelve leads that agree
fourteen, febrile, a rub, and elevation in every lead — this is not a plumbing problem. look at the shape again.
admitted for rest, the echo repeated tomorrow — sport can wait a month

outcomes.label: Read off twelve leads, treated with tablets — home to rest, echo booked
The needle beat the bleed — alive, with a scar that was never needed
Tamponade — the lytic found the one chest it should never touch
